_about: How the pathfinder prices a trip before traffic exists. Road segments take their free-flow speed from their type in roads.json. Rail and path segments have no types until M7 and M8, so each network gets one speed here, in km/h. Both are placeholders with no source, there only so a route filtered to rail or path has a cost. M5 replaces free-flow time with congested time.

rail.source: Placeholder. A rough average for urban rail with stops, until M7 gives rail its own types.

path.source: Placeholder. Walking pace, until M8 gives paths their own types.

travelTimes._about: Free-flow travel times between zones (issue #177). The map is cut into 500 m zones, one per chunk, and a table holds the drive between every two of them. sameZoneSeconds is the time given two buildings in one zone, so a pop can work next door. A change of roads rebuilds the table over ticks: rebuildSettlesPerTick is how many road nodes the rebuild may settle in a tick, counted as zones with a road times the road nodes in the city, so the tick it is ready by follows from state alone. 32,000 is about 2.5 ms on the development container, kept low because the soak, at 4x with the page beside it, ran slices about three times slower: the 30,000 segment city, 440 zones with a road and 18,500 road nodes, rebuilds over about 260 ticks.
